source.name: EDTF specification examples (Library of Congress)
source.attribution: Extended Date/Time Format (EDTF) Specification, Library of Congress, February 2019 (ISO 8601-2:2019 profile). Example strings as published; descriptions paraphrased. See THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md.
source.notes: The specification's own examples, level by level. Our canonical form is EDTF wherever EDTF can say the thing, so the expected canonical is the EDTF string itself where we support the feature; entries for features we do not yet support (times of day, unspecified months and days, set members with '..', 'all members' sets, exponential and significant-digit years, component-level qualifiers) expect 'unparsed' and document the gap. Held at proposed as an imported file.

entries.notes: EDTF distinguishes an unknown end ('/') from an open one ('/..'); we treat both as open.

EDTF reads this as 1986 BCE; the default profile's LeadingDashIsOpenStart reads free text '-1985' as an open start and keeps the EDTF reading as an alternative. A profile with the policy off gives '-1985'.
